summary: Redwood ran a demo of the Model Catalog, focusing on how Graystone Health can select open models, review benchmark results, and map compatibility across their on-prem and cloud GPU fleet. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment for compliance-sensitive EHR workflows; main concerns were latency, cost, and compatibility with quantized models on H100/T4. Agreed to run a POC benchmark with sample prompts and share detailed compatibility matrix and pricing.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-04 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46 minutes | Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Tanya (Product), Rajiv, Lena, Tommy, Sophie (Graystone)

Summary: quick walkthrough of model catalog UI, demo of benchmarking page, Q&A about GPU compat matrices and on-prem support.

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time today, um we'll do a 30 minute demo and leave time for q and a, Marco is going to show the model catalog console and some benchmark pages.
[00:22] Rajiv: great thanks, yeah we wanted to see how we can pick open models and understand perf for our workflows, we have both H100s on prem and some cloud T4s for burst.
[00:35] Marco: perfect, that's exactly what we'll cover. quick intro — model catalog is a curated list of open models with verified performance profiles, quality scores, and compatibility notes. you'll see recommended quantization and kernel mappings per GPU.
[01:05] Lena: when you say "verified" what does that mean? are these Redwood runs or community numbers?
[01:12] Marco: mostly Redwood-run benchmarks on standard prompts, plus community contributions flagged separately. we run token-latency, throughput, and memory profiles using a consistent harness. small note — the transcriptions, sorry the numbers can vary by seq length and prompt shape.
[01:35] Tommy: and are the benchmarks for both FP16 and 4-bit quantized variants? we want to understand the tradeoffs.
[01:42] Marco: yes, we include FP16, int8 and 4-bit q4 variants where supported. the catalog displays expected latency deltas and an estimated quality delta from an internal eval set.
[02:10] [screen share shift noise] Marco: okay opening the catalog — top left is filters: task (chat, completion, embedding), model family, license, and performance tier. here i filter for open-license models with strong chat performance.
[02:45] Marco: you'll see model cards with a perf ribbon — p50 latency @ 512 tokens on A100, throughput numbers, and a small quality bar. click a model and you get a compatibility matrix.
[03:10] Aisha: can you show the matrix for the 'Mistral-Open-XL' variant? we asked about its performance previously.
[03:24] Marco: sure — opening Mistral-Open-XL. matrix shows tested GPUs across top (H100, A100, T4) and quantization columns (FP16, int8, q4). 
[03:42] Marco: for H100: FP16 p50 ~ 45ms/token, q4 p50 ~ 70ms/token but cost drops ~2.1x. for T4 the model needs more memory tricks, we recommend int8 for throughput — p50 goes up but cost is lower. exact numbers are on the bench page exported as CSV.
[04:12] Lena: how reliable are quality estimates when you quantize to q4? we can't have hallucination regressions for EHR extraction tasks.
[04:24] Marco: good question — we provide a small delta score from our eval suite; for many LLMs q4 keeps >98% of key-entity F1 on extraction tasks but it depends on the prompt. recommended approach — run a short POC with your prompts. we've noted models with large deltas in the catalog.
[05:00] Rajiv: working through our constraints, we need single-digit ms latency on short prompts for routing decisions. are you seeing those numbers on any open models?
[05:12] Marco: single-digit ms per token is rare for large open models at typical seq lengths unless you use specialized kernels and very short contexts; we can get low end-to-end latency with smaller models or aggressive batching policies and prefix caching. we'll highlight candidates.
[05:45] Sophie: security check — if we use Redwood Private in our VPC, do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration for key wrap? also audit logs?
[05:58] Tanya: yes, Private supports KMS integrations and we can route logs to your SIEM. we also offer audit logs and RBAC, and can support a scoping call with our security team.
[06:25] Tommy: for on-prem H100s, what's the recommended quantization/compilation stack? our infra team runs containers with CUDA 12 and custom drivers.
[06:40] Marco: we typically recommend compiling via our runtime which selects optimized kernels; for H100 we prefer FP16 for lowest latency, but if you need cost savings q4 with kernel tuning is viable. we have an input field in the matrix for driver/OS notes — we also publish known-good driver combos.
[07:05] [noise] Marco: jumping to the bench page, you can see histograms by token length and p50/p95 numbers, also a per-token cost estimate based on instance hourly cost.
[07:30] Rajiv: can you overlay our expected qps so we can see tail latency effects?
[07:36] Marco: yes — there's a "simulate" tool; you can enter qps and sequence distribution. i'll demo with 100 qps and 75/25 short/long split.
[08:00] Marco: simulation shows p95 increases non-linearly with qps; with batching we get better throughput but higher tail. recommended is a dedicated pool for critical paths.
[08:28] Aisha: quick question for Lena — what's your expected throughput and latency SLOs for the EHR routing use case?
[08:38] Lena: for routing, target is 200 qps with 95th < 250ms and cost under our threshold. for summarization batch jobs we can tolerate higher latency.
[08:52] Marco: okay that helps, we can propose a Mixed pool: small models on hosted for non-sensitive workloads, Private/dedicated for PII.
[09:20] Sophie: regarding data residency — we need logs to remain in our region and retention policies. is that supported in Private?
[09:30] Tanya: yes Private keeps control plane in your VPC and you can configure retention. for hosted we'd need a contract addendum for residency.
[09:50] [10:00] Marco: moving on — model vetting: each model card includes license, maintainer, benchmark notes, and usage caveats; e.g., some models have Apache-style permissive licenses vs more restrictive ones.
[10:30] Rajiv: do you have a default recommendation for model families for entity extraction vs conversational triage?
[10:38] Marco: for extraction smaller encoder-decoder or specialized fine-tuned open models often win cost/latency. for conversational triage medium-sized chat models in the catalog with strong safety filters are preferred.
[11:05] Lena: about fine-tuning — can we bring our own finetuned checkpoints into the catalog? how does compatibility work?
[11:15] Marco: yes you can upload a model artifact in Private; we validate architecture and then run a compatibility test on your target hardware to generate a matrix entry. that process is part of our onboarding.
[11:40] Tommy: can that validation run on our cluster or does Redwood need artifacts? we prefer to keep checkpoints in-house.
[11:50] Marco: we support two flows: you can run the validation harness in your environment and upload the results, or you can give us temporary access under NDA for us to run it. many enterprises choose the former.
[12:12] [12:30] Aisha: quick demo of the Optimize tab — this suggests batching thresholds, cache TTLs, and quantization recommendations by workload.
[12:45] Marco: Optimize will recommend an autoscaling policy and a quantization profile. for example it may recommend q4 on T4 for embeddings and FP16 on H100 for chat.
[13:10] Rajiv: we saw an interesting note in your docs about "fallback policies" — can you explain how that works in production if a model is overloaded?
[13:20] Tanya: fallback policies let you route to a compatible model variant (e.g., lower-cost model or hosted fallback) automatically when Dedicated pool is saturated. you can configure SLO-based thresholds for failover.
[13:45] Sophie: from a security standpoint, how are fallbacks audited? we need trail for which model served which request.
[13:55] Tanya: audit logs include route decisions and model variant used per request id. we can export to your log store.
[14:20] Marco: demoing the benchmark CSV export — here's a CSV with p50/p95 per sequence bucket, memory footprint, and kernel notes.
[14:40] Lena: perfect, can you show an example for a long-context model? we are interested in 8k token contexts for clinical notes.
[14:52] Marco: here's LlamaX-8k, p50 for 2048 tokens on A100 is ~210ms/token, memory footprint is high; we recommend kv caching for repeated prefixes to lower cost.
[15:20] Rajiv: kv caching — how transparent is it and what about privacy implications?
[15:30] Marco: caching can be enabled per-route; in Private deployments cache stays in your VPC. for hosted we offer encrypted caches and TTL controls. caching is optional for PHI-sensitive data.
[15:58] Tommy: what's typical cost reduction from cache?
[16:05] Marco: can be 20-60% depending on prefix reuse. the Optimize tab simulates savings.
[16:30] Aisha: ok let's go through a concrete POC plan — propose 2-3 candidate models, run benchmarks on your sample prompts across H100 and T4, and then compare quality/latency/cost.
[16:45] Lena: yes that aligns. we'll provide sample prompt sets for routing and extraction.
[16:55] Marco: i'll note that — recommended candidates: Mistral-Open-XL (cost-optimized chat), LlamaX-8k (long context), and Falcon-Complement (smaller extraction model).
[17:20] Rajiv: any licensing concerns with those models? we need to ensure no restrictive clauses for clinical use.
[17:30] Marco: the catalog flags licenses; we'll double-check, but the ones mentioned are permissive for commercial use; we'll include legal notes in the matrix.
[17:55] [18:10] Sophie: also, does Redwood provide a data processing addendum for PHI?
[18:18] Tanya: yes we have DPA templates and can discuss HIPAA-related addenda on Private deployments.
[18:35] Marco: showing the compatibility matrix export — you can filter by kernel support (triton, custom CUDA kernels), and see which kernels produce best latency on given driver versions.
[19:05] Tommy: our stack uses custom driver 535 and CUDA 12 — any known issues?
[19:15] Marco: we'll include a "known-good" mapping for your driver combo; if not, we run a quick driver validation as part of POC.
[19:40] Aisha: question about multitenancy — if we run Dedicated, can we pin model versions and enforce per-route policies?
[19:50] Tanya: yes, Dedicated pools can be configured with pinned model versions and route-level policies including rate limits and quotas.
[20:10] Rajiv: what about rollback and canary deploys for model updates?
[20:20] Marco: rollouts are supported — you can do canary percentages and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected per your eval set.
[20:50] Lena: will Redwood run the regression checks or do we host the eval harness?
[20:58] Tanya: we provide tooling; customers can host their own evals and integrate results into the rollout policy. many teams use both.
[21:20] [21:40] Marco: demoing the API quickstart — show the endpoints for model list, bench data, and simulate. here's an example fetch for model metadata and compatibility matrix.
[22:05] Marco: note: the metadata contains 'recommended_container' and 'quant_profiles' fields — that helps infra configure runtime.
[22:30] Tommy: can we point our orchestration to a YAML config generated by Redwood?
[22:38] Marco: yes the console can export deployment manifests and suggested runtime flags.
[22:55] Rajiv: about cost — what's the expected cost reduction compared to running vanilla large model on H100 without quantization or caching?
[23:05] Marco: depends, but typical wins are 2-5x by using quantization, batching, and cache. Optimize shows estimated per-request savings.
[23:45] Lena: for the POC, can we get token-level cost breakdown and latency traces? that's important for our SRE.
[23:55] Marco: yes, Redwood Console provides per-request token breakdowns and traces you can export. we'll include sample traces in the follow-up.
[24:20] [24:40] Aisha: any other questions on model selection before we move to logistics?
[24:48] Rajiv: curious — do you have benchmarks for instruction-following vs base models?
[24:56] Marco: yes we benchmark both; instruction-tuned models typically have slightly higher latency but better downstream accuracy for chat tasks. we'll include those comparisons.
[25:20] Sophie: for auditability, can model provenance be tracked (who uploaded which model and when)?
[25:30] Tanya: yes, audit logs include provenance metadata and we support immutable model registry entries.
[25:50] Marco: jumping to the recommended POC plan in the console — step 1: provide prompts; step 2: Redwood runs bench on your fleet or you run harness; step 3: compare quality metrics and pick final candidate; step 4: pilot with dedicated pool.
[26:20] Lena: timeline wise we want results in two weeks. is that realistic?
[26:28] Aisha: yes if we get prompts by next week we can schedule bench runs and have outputs in ~10 business days.
[26:40] Marco: also note, for private deployments there is setup lead time — we'll send estimated timelines.
[27:05] [27:30] Rajiv: one more nit — do you support model sharding or tensor parallel strategies in the runtime?
[27:40] Marco: runtime supports model parallelism and kernel-level sharding; we abstract those details but can expose knobs if you want to tune.
[28:05] Tommy: any caveats for small batch sizes? our traffic is spiky with many single-request users.
[28:16] Marco: small batches favor latency but cost increases; Optimize suggests burst pools and autoscale thresholds to manage spikiness.
[28:40] Aisha: let's review the concrete deliverables — compatibility matrix, pricing, security docs, POC schedule.
[28:50] Aisha: Marco and I will follow up with the matrix and pricing; Lena to send prompts; Sophie to send security questions.
[29:10] [29:30] Marco: quick live note — adding a remark about expected seq length distribution and qps into the simulate tool.
[29:48] Rajiv: ok, as long as we can see p95s with our distribution that's good.
[30:00] Marco: demo wrap up — open to questions.
[30:10] Lena: two quick ones: 1) is there an SLA for Dedicated latency? 2) what's the max context you support experimentally?
[30:22] Tanya: SLA varies by contract but Dedicated has latency SLOs we can bake in. max context depends on model, we support up to 64k in some experimental builds but production support needs validation.
[30:45] Marco: also note that long context models require different kv cache strategies.
[31:12] [31:30] Sophie: for the POC, can Redwood sign a BAA or HIPAA DPA?
[31:40] Aisha: yes on Private deployments we can discuss BAA; for hosted we have additional controls and would need legal review.
[32:05] Rajiv: any red flags we should watch for when moving from demo to POC?
[32:15] Marco: main ones: mismatched seq distributions, driver incompatibilities, and license surprises — we surface all in the matrix.
[32:40] Lena: ok good.
[32:50] Marco: showing the export config — you get a zip with CSVs and a YAML manifest and a README that lists known caveats.
[33:15] Aisha: we'll send that export after the call.
[33:30] [33:50] Marco: final quick note on fallbacks — you can set per-route model chains, e.g., primary on Dedicated and fallback to hosted lower-cost model. there is a small added latency on the switch but it's automatic.
[34:15] Tommy: how do you measure quality regression to trigger rollback? is it strictly eval-based or can we use production telemetry?
[34:28] Tanya: both; rollouts can use eval metrics or production monitors and you can set thresholds for rollback triggers.
[34:55] Rajiv: ok this is helpful. wrapping up — we'll aim to send prompts and security questions by next Tuesday.
[35:10] Aisha: great — we'll follow up with matrix, pricing, and a proposed POC schedule.
[35:25] Lena: thanks everyone.
[35:35] Sophie: thanks, appreciate it.
[35:45] Aisha: thanks all, end call.

Post-call notes: agreed to a POC focusing on three candidate models and benchmark runs on H100 and T4; deliverables include compatibility matrix, pricing, security docs, and timeline.
